## Why

I chose a shepherd’s crook or crozier as the single recognizable subject for *Si Diligis*. This object perfectly encapsulates the encyclical’s core message regarding pastoral authority, vigilance, and the hierarchy of the Magisterium. As the standard attribute of a bishop, the crozier symbolizes the divinely-instituted authority and the duty to guard the flock against "spiritual contagion," reinforcing that teaching must conform to episcopal oversight. It is immediately recognizable and inherently symbolic, avoiding abstraction while powerfully conveying the document’s focus on the shepherd’s duty of governance and teaching.

## Text-to-image prompt
```text
A premium 3D render of a magnificent, single shepherd’s crozier, crafted from polished gold and silver, standing upright on a simple, dark circular plinth. The crook is richly ornamented with intricate scrollwork and filigree, ending in a stylized, jewel-encrusted spiral that symbolizes the bishop's authority. The shaft has a detailed texture of hammered metal and fine etching, with a few small, deeply embedded gems. The sculpture is rendered with physically based materials, global illumination, and pronounced ambient occlusion, capturing the realistic reflections and micro-surface details of the metals. The crozier is positioned dead-center in the frame, viewed frontally at mid-height with an 85mm lens equivalent and f/11 aperture, ensuring a symmetrical composition and full visibility. The background is completely transparent. Dramatic high-contrast lighting comes from above-front-left, casting deep shadows and strong highlights that emphasize the sculptural form and texture. A subtle rim light from the rear-right carves the silhouette against the void. There is no text, lettering, or other objects in the image, preserving a clean, sacred-object aesthetic.
```
